dossier.public_summary: The dip appears strongly on a subset of transits and disappears or flips sign in others, with depths that swing from zero to over 1000 ppm. Individual transits are highly inconsistent and much of the folded signal is carried by a few outliers, unlike a stable planet transit. Together with a significant secondary dip similar in depth and a non-stable depth pattern, this favours an eclipsing/false-positive/blend over a planet.

reasons.why: Depth changes dramatically between sectors (and within one product) so the signal is not stable, argues against a coherent transit on the target.
SPOC 2-min alone shows highly inconsistent depths: near 1000 ppm then consistent with zero, typical of systematics/blend, not a planet.
